guarantees.claim: On asynchronous reset (rst_ni low), key_state_q is cleared to 0 and all words of key_state_ecc_q are set to the ECC check bits for all-zero data (SecdedInv7264ZeroEcc).

When not in reset (rst_ni high), all CDIs*Shares*EccWords entries of key_state_ecc_q are updated every cycle with the encoded output of the corresponding entry from key_state_ecc_words_d using prim_secded_inv_72_64_enc.
key_state_q is assigned only during reset; when rst_ni is high, this block never updates key_state_q, so it retains the reset value (0) unless driven by another process.
guarantees.cond: rst_ni is high after reset deassertion

assumptions.claim: TotalEccWords must equal the product CDIs * Shares * EccWords to ensure the reset replication covers all and only the words that will be updated later; otherwise, a subset of words may be left uninitialized or the array may be overfilled.
assumptions.risk: After reset, some ECC words retain unpredictable values if TotalEccWords < CDIs*Shares*EccWords, violating data integrity assumption of the key state storage. If TotalEccWords is larger, the reset value may exceed the declared dimensions, causing a parameter mismatch or simulation/synthesis error.

assumptions.risk: A width mismatch could cause silent truncation or loss of ECC check bits, compromising error detection/correction integrity.

security_implications: This chunk manages key state with ECC integrity protection. key_state_q is a plaintext key state register that is zeroed at reset and never written again (G3), potentially leaving the key state stuck at zero if it is the sole source of the current key value. If key_state_ecc_q holds the actual ECC-encoded key material, its continuous update from key_state_ecc_words_d is security-critical: any width mismatch in reset replication (A1) or encoding function (A2) could compromise ECC integrity, leading to undetected corruption of key data. The forced zero on key_state_q may be either an intentional zeroization or an oversight; in either case, the behavior of key_state_q after reset directly impacts key availability and confidentiality.
